name: folio

scripts.pages:build: VITE_BASE=/folio/ npm run build && node tools/stamp-sw.mjs dist
scripts.author: node --experimental-strip-types tools/authoring/cli.ts
scripts.coverage:all: mkdir -p .coverage && { npm run coverage:unit >.coverage/unit.log 2>&1 || { cat .coverage/unit.log; exit 1; }; } && { npm run e2e >.coverage/e2e.log 2>&1 || { cat .coverage/e2e.log; exit 1; }; } && node tools/coverage-report.mjs --per-file

comment:coverage-combined: Combined coverage measured 97.87-97.92% over six runs (2026-10-31): five on the dev box and one in CI. It then rose to 98.00-98.04% once the e2e collected uncaught errors properly and three vacuous assertions were replaced with real ones. Floor is 97.5: 0.35pp below the lowest figure ever observed (97.85) and about 1.5x the measured 0.23pp band. The margin is deliberate and larger than the 0.06pp the old floor used: CON-COV-002 forbids lowering a floor, so an over-tight one has to be walked back and an over-loose one merely ratchets again. Drift, measured rather than inferred: the COMBINED figure has been observed between 97.85% and 98.08% across twenty runs (ten here and two in CI when this was first written, plus eight more across review rounds 5-11, which moved the TOP of the band to 98.08 as those rounds added tests). Re-measured rather than left behind: a recorded band that the current run already sits outside is a measurement going stale, and this repo's whole argument for the floor rests on the band being real. The LOWER bound is what the floor is set from and it has not moved. That is a 0.23pp band, about 20 lines of 8807 (it read 0.21pp and 18 lines until the band was re-measured, and the two sentences then disagreed with each other inside one note). Underneath it the BROWSER half swings far more, 3965-4089 covered lines over six runs, because a session that renders slightly differently or a check that retries moves a hundred lines; most of that is absorbed by the union, since the unit half already covers those lines. src/shader.ts itself varies by three lines (150-153). An earlier version of this note said the three-line shader figure WAS the drift, which inferred the whole from one file (CON-DATA-001) — and it is the number the headroom argument rests on. The thing that USED to drift — destroy() and the webglcontextlost handler, 13 lines, once in three runs — is deterministic now: the e2e fires WEBGL_lose_context.loseContext() rather than hoping a page detaches the canvas before closing. The recorded cause for that swing (headless Chrome refusing a WebGL context) was wrong; a probe granted one 9 times out of 9. Never raise this on a single run.
comment:coverage-logs: coverage:all keeps the unit and e2e output in .coverage/*.log and CATS IT ON FAILURE, so a failing run prints its own diagnosis and a passing one stays quiet. Two earlier attempts were both wrong, in opposite directions. Redirecting to a file alone was worse than /dev/null in CI: .coverage is gitignored and the runner workspace is discarded, so the output stopped being visible anywhere. Piping to tee restored visibility and SILENTLY BROKE THE GATE — npm runs scripts under sh, which has no pipefail, so the pipeline reports tee status and a red e2e exited 0. run.mjs writes browser.lcov before process.exit(1), so the coverage figure would have looked almost normal and the job would have gone green on a broken e2e (CON-VER-001). `cmd >log || { cat log; exit 1; }` keeps the status and the output both.
comment:coverage-floor: coverage:gate hardcodes the floor rather than relying on `npm run X -- --min N`. The passthrough is npm-version dependent: it applied in CI and silently did NOT apply locally, which would have left the gate unable to fail after an npm upgrade. Hardcode, like test:gate.
comment:coverage: test:gate floors are a RATCHET — raise them in the PR that earns the improvement, never lower them to make a build green (CON-COV-002). These are the UNIT-only floors; the combined floor lives in coverage:gate and is documented above. Baseline 38.91/74.52/39.41 set 2026-09-20 when import-all first forced the whole of src/ into the denominator (the previously reported 87.65% measured only five files). Phase 1 raised it to 86.05/71.67/75.42 — branches fell because newly-covered files brought their unexercised branches into the denominator, which is the honest direction. Ratcheted again 2026-10-31 to 95.5/89/80. MEASURE BEFORE YOU TRUST THE NUMBERS BELOW, with `for i in 1 2 3; do npm run test:coverage; done` — they are a snapshot of one commit, not a property of the suite. Eight runs at the head of PR #74 give lines 96.06 and functions 89.64 every time, branches 80.34-80.48, so the floors sit 0.56pp, 0.64pp and 0.34pp under the measured minima and BRANCHES is the thin one. This note has now gone stale three times inside one PR, each time because a later commit added lines to src/ and nobody re-ran it: it claimed 95.99 lines when the suite gave 96.04, then 96.04 when review round 13's error-handling in search.ts and palette.ts had moved it to 95.92, and each stale copy read as a measurement. The lesson is the one cdp.mjs learned about hand-maintained counts - a figure that must be re-typed to stay true is a liability - except that here the figures ARE the argument for the floor, so they cannot simply be dropped. Hence the command, first. The branch wobble itself is NOT a flaky test: BRH (branches HIT) is constant while BRF (branches COUNTED) varies by one in src/fx.ts, so nothing the suite executes changes and this is V8's denominator - a measurement artifact to leave margin for, not a CON-VER-008 suite defect to fix. Raise the branch floor only off a freshly measured minimum, and prefer earning the room back by covering some of fx.ts's unhit branches (task 24 in specs/015-delight). This field used to say "Destination is 95" and "remaining climb to 95 needs browser-side coverage (shader/engine/tilt)": both were left standing after the combined floor passed 95 and reached 97.5, so the record contradicted the gate it describes — the same stale-note failure task 14c was closed for.
comment:author: The AI authoring pipeline (npm run author) needs @anthropic-ai/sdk. Install it on demand — `npm i -D @anthropic-ai/sdk` — it is not part of the app build.
